translation_notes: Two DIFFERENT namespace sources in the same file, translated two DIFFERENT ways -- this is the finding this region contributes to the stratum. `from tests import BASE_URI` is a genuine project-owned namespace module (tests/__init__.py: `BASE_URI = Namespace('http://example.com/')`): the context shim (orm_context.py) reproduces it and additionally exports `__namespaces__ = {"base": BASE_URI}`, which is what makes `from orm_context import base:` work -- one line added to a module we already had to shim. `from rdflib.namespace import RDF, OWL` is NOT project-owned: it is rdflib itself, a real pinned external dependency we cannot and must not patch to add `__namespaces__`. Verified: `from rdflib.namespace import rdf:` raises ImportError (cannot import name '__namespaces__' from 'rdflib.namespace') -- rdflib.namespace.RDF/OWL are ordinary module attributes, not a `__namespaces__` dict. So RDF/OWL fall back to `@prefix rdf:`/`@prefix owl:`, module-scoped right after the unchanged plain import -- this is exactly the cost the AGENT_BATCH point-dur predicted: the IRI (here two well-known W3C IRIs) gets typed out at this call site instead of being read off the shared rdflib binding. Cheap for RDF/OWL (stable, famous IRIs) but the failure mode generalises badly: any third-party namespace module (a vocab package on PyPI, a library's own `NS = Namespace(...)`) hits the same wall, and only the IMPORTING project can work around it by shimming/vendoring its OWN namespace modules with `__namespaces__` -- it cannot fix someone else's package.

the two DefinedNamespace-alias cases documented for this stratum (Display-Lab/scaffold's PSDO, CPO) do not arise here: RDF.type/RDF.value/OWL.Thing/BASE_URI.test are plain Namespace attribute access, readable-name == local-name, so @prefix and the project import are both faithful.

rdf_ops/categories count 21 namespace_term + graph_ctor/graph_read/term_constructor across FIVE separate pytest test_* functions, none invoked by a bare exec of the file (pytest discovers and calls them; module-state comparison sees zero graphs and empty stdout on both sides regardless of translation correctness). driver.py is therefore custom, not the generic run_pair(entry=None): it calls each test_* in file order on both sides and compares outcome (completed vs raised, and the exception type) plus stdout per call -- the tests' own internal asserts (g.value(...) == URIRef('123'), pytest.raises(...)) do the isomorphism-equivalent checking. Negative control run: swapping base:test for base:wrong in one read makes test_irifield_convert_to_rdf disagree (original ok vs translated AssertionError), confirming the driver is sensitive to the translation, not just to the shim.

CONFIRMED upstream fragility, reproduced identically rather than fixed: Database.databases is a shared class attribute never reset between the shim's tests, and the first two tests (test_required_field_raises, test_irifield_create) never call Database.set_db() themselves. Run standalone -- `pytest tests/fields/test_irifield.py` against the checked-out repo at corpus/repos/edmondchuc__rdflib-orm -- BOTH raise AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'base_uri' instead of the FieldError/success their bodies read as if expected; they only pass inside the full suite because an earlier test file happens to set the 'default' Database first. The driver resets Database.databases before each side's five-call run (both sides import the same cached orm_context module, so Database is literally the same class object) and reproduces the AttributeError identically on both sides -- this is the region's own bug, not a translation defect, and the protocol says not to fix it.

classification minor-restructuring, not directly-expressible: the import block is restructured (BASE_URI's own import line folds into the models/base: import; two @prefix lines are inserted) to give from … import p: and @prefix each their own coherent block -- a straight line-for-line substitution was not possible once two different namespace sources needed two different constructions.
